name: feedback-channel-benchmark
description: "Online forecasters increasingly adapt after deployment from targets as they arrive, yet evaluation treats an arrived target as both supervision and ground truth. When feedback is delayed, stale, or corrupted, that conflation hides whether failure came from corruption, temporal change, or fewer update opportunities. We introduce a causal benchmark separating the target exposed to adaptation from the clean target reserved for scoring, enforcing horizon-aware availability, and pairing native with controlled update exposure. The evaluation spans five data sets, two backbones, and three methods. Corruption effects prove method-and-execution-path dependent: pronounced for COSA natively, smaller for TAFAS, null or reversed for Proceed. A 32\/64\/96\/native curve makes COSA sensitivity descriptively monotone, while $5\\times5$ crossed-seed panels leave Proceed uncertain. On four audited COSA cells at 24-hour delay we compare a median-absolute-deviation (MAD) filter, two robust-loss settings, and a selection rule taken from the literature against a non-deployable mask oracle that recovers 95\\%--101\\% of the corruption-induced excess error. The filter earns a prevalence-adjusted detection lift on Weather yet no gain anywhere; the robust losses convert 11%--26% and tax clean adaptation. The literature rule converts 89\\% and 95\\% on ETTh2 with gains excluding zero and no resolved clean tax, but only 23% and 24% on Weather.
